children.text: saṃkrāmo 'tra na bhāvanā na ca kathāyuktir na carcā na ca
dhyānaṃ vā na ca dhāraṇā na ca japābhyāsaprayāso na ca |
children.translated_text: nor by <s>dhyāna</s> (meditative absorption), nor by <s>dhāraṇā</s> (fixation), nor by the toil of practicing <s>japa</s> (muttering repetition);
Here, there is no passage by <s>bhāvanā</s> (contemplative cultivation), nor by the logic of discourse, nor by discussion,

children.text: tat kiṃ nāma suniścitaṃ vada paraṃ satyaṃ ca tacchrūyatāṃ
na tyāgī na parigrahī bhaja sukhaṃ sarvaṃ yathāvasthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: be neither a renouncer nor an acquisitor; enjoy ease while everything remains just as it is.
then what, indeed, is firmly ascertained? speak; let that supreme truth be heard,

children.text: saṃsāro 'sti na tattvatas tanubhṛtāṃ bandhasya vārtaiva kā
bandho yasya na jātu tasya vitathā muktasya muktikriyā |
children.translated_text: For one who has never had bondage, the doing of <s>mukti</s> (liberation) is vain;
There is no <s>saṃsāra</s> (cycle of existence) in reality; for embodied beings, what talk at all of <s>bandha</s> (bondage)?

children.text: mithyāmohakṛd eṣa rajjubhujagacchāyāpiśācabhramo mā kiṃcit tyaja

children.translated_text: do not grasp; roam at ease, self-possessed, just as things are.
this delusive error—like the illusion of a snake in a rope, like a goblin of a shadow—do not abandon anything,

children.text: kila kasya kena vidadhe ko vā praveśakramaḥ |
children.translated_text: who indeed accomplishes what for whom, and what could any procedure of entry be?
What is this chain of distinctions—<s>pūjā</s> (worship), <s>pūjaka</s> (worshiper), and <s>pūjya</s> (the worshiped)? what talk is there of a “passage” into the <s>anuttara</s> (the unsurpassed),

children.text: māyeyam na cidadvayāt paratayā bhinnāpy aho vartate sarvaṃ

children.translated_text: do not make vain <s>cintā</s> (mental elaboration); it is pure, being of the nature of one’s own direct experience.
This is <s>māyā</s> (cosmic illusion): not separate from <s>cidadvaya</s> (nondual consciousness), even while appearing distinct as “other”, ah, all goes on,
nor is the rise of illumination like a heap of radiance produced by lamp, sun, and moon;
Here <s>ānanda</s> (bliss) is not of the sort from wealth, from drink, nor like the embrace of a woman,
the dawning of illumination is the attainment of the treasure that had been forgotten: the station of <s>sarvādvaita</s> (the nonduality of all).
joy is the ground of the happiness of release from accumulated difference—like the unloading of a burden,
though they appear, are not of a nature different from the body of the universe,
Those states—arising and subsiding of attraction and aversion, pleasure and pain, <s>ahaṅkāra</s> (egoity), dejection, and the like—

children.text: vyaktiṃ paśyasi yasya yasya sahasā tattattadekātmatāsaṃvidrūpam

children.translated_text: seeing thus, why do you not rejoice, brimming with that <s>bhāvanā</s> (contemplation)?
whatever manifestation you behold, at once see it as <s>saṃvid</s> (awareness) in the form of <s>ekātmatā</s> (one-identity) of each and every thing,

children.text: pūrvābhāvabhavakriyā hi sahasā bhāvāḥ sadā 'smin bhave

children.translated_text: mixed with intermediate forms and modifications—whence reality for them?
For the states that, here, ever suddenly arise are processes of becoming out of prior non-existence,
go beyond doubt, fear, blemish, scheming contrivance; be awakened.
In the fickle, unreal heap of <s>prapañca</s> (manifold proliferation), in the variegated dream-illusion,

children.text: bhāvānāṃ na samudbhavo 'sti sahajas tvadbhāvitā bhānty amī
niḥsatyā api satyatām anubhavabhrāntyā bhajanti kṣaṇam |
children.translated_text: though devoid of reality, by the delusion of experience they assume reality for a moment,
There is no origination of states; it is their innate being-conceived-by-you that makes them appear,

children.text: tvatsaṅkalpaja eṣa viśvamahimā nāsty asya janmānyataḥ
tasmāt tvaṃ vibhavena bhāsi bhuvaneṣv ekopy anekātmakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: therefore you shine forth by your power in the worlds—one, yet of manifold nature.
this majesty of the universe is born of your <s>saṅkalpa</s> (intentional projection); it has no other birth,

children.text: yat satyaṃ yad asatyam alpabahulaṃ nityaṃ na nityaṃ ca yat
yan māyāmalinaṃ yad ātmavimalaṃ ciddarpaṇe rājate |
children.translated_text: what is tainted by <s>māyā</s> and what is pure as <s>ātman</s> (Self) shines in the mirror of <s>cit</s> (consciousness),
What is true and what untrue, what little and what abundant, what eternal and what not eternal,
assume lordship over the universe, your greatness established upon your own direct experience.
knowing all that, from the arising of <s>svavimarśa-saṃvid</s> (reflexive consciousness), to be of the nature of forms revealed,
Thus ends the Anuttarāṣṭikā composed by the venerable teacher <s>Abhinavagupta</s>.
[1] variant: vilasa.
